title: Widest Vertical Area Between Two Points Containing No Points
summary: Given n points on a 2D plane, find the maximum width of a vertical area between two points where no other points lie within the area.
statement: Given n points on a 2D plane, find the maximum width of a vertical area between two points where no other points lie within the area. A vertical area extends infinitely along the y-axis and the widest area is defined by the greatest distance between any two x-coordinates, excluding points on the edge.
constraints: At least two points with integer coordinates; several points may share an x-coordinate.
Return the greatest difference between adjacent distinct sorted x-coordinates. Points on the two boundary lines are allowed.
hints: Only horizontal positions matter because the open area extends infinitely vertically.
Sort all x-coordinates and inspect adjacent gaps.
Extract x, sort, and maximize each next minus previous value.
Any strip wider than an adjacent sorted gap would contain another x-coordinate; every adjacent gap has an empty interior.
editorial: Any strip wider than an adjacent sorted gap would contain another x-coordinate; every adjacent gap has an empty interior.

tests.explanation: Distinct x-coordinates are seven, eight, and nine, so the widest empty strip has width one.
The largest adjacent x gap is from three to five, with width two.
